title: FinOps: the bill
description: One bill in the shape of a FinOps tool: AWS from the cost exporter, fixed costs by hand (the Claude plan among them), Claude Code API calls from Loki at list price while the plan has no price; the plan against list price; cost centers by rule, this month against last, movers, anomalies, unit costs, record types. Periods: AWS is the UTC calendar month to date, the Claude Code sums follow the dashboard's range in the browser's timezone (the plan row is pinned to the calendar month), fixed costs are per month; with the default range (this month) they line up to within hours, with another range an unpriced plan's bill adds that range's calls to this month's AWS. Internal; not shared.

panels.title: One bill
panels.description: AWS month to date, plus the fixed costs entered in fixed-costs.json, plus the Claude Code API calls in the dashboard's range at their list price only while the Claude subscription has no price. Once it is priced, the plan is one of the fixed costs and is the Claude term; the list price stays out of the bill and shows in the next row for comparison. Added server side with a Grafana expression: PromQL's or cannot reach the Loki series, and the expression keeps the three sources apart.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: AWS, month to date
panels.description: Unblended cost from the 1st (UTC) to now, today's partial cost included. The source lags by hours: the report lands up to three times a day.

panels.title: Claude Code API calls, list price
panels.description: What the API calls in the range would cost at list price, from Claude Code's own api_request events. The subscription covers them. The bill counts this amount only while the subscription has no price; the next row sets it against the plan.

panels.title: Fixed costs entered
panels.description: Monthly subscriptions and seats from fixed-costs.json, the Claude plan included once it has a price. Items without a price are counted on the data row below and left out here.

panels.title: AWS vs last month, same days
panels.description: Complete days 1 to N of this month against days 1 to N of last month (N on the data row). Positive is up. A domain renewal or the monthly tax in one window and not the other shows here.

panels.title: Forecast / budget
panels.description: Month-end forecast against the MONTHLY budget in AWS Budgets: the run rate of this month's complete days in report mode, Cost Explorer's forecast otherwise (the data row names the method). Red above 100%.

panels.title: Plan price this month
panels.description: The monthly price of the Claude subscription: the item named in fixed-costs.json, entered in the git-ignored fixed-costs.local.json. It reads Not priced until the item has an amount.

panels.title: List price, month to date
panels.description: What the Claude Code API calls since the first of the month would cost at list price. List price is what Claude Code reports per call (cost_usd on its api_request events, summed in Loki). The panel is pinned to the calendar month in the browser's timezone, whatever range the dashboard shows.

panels.title: List price, month-end projection
panels.description: Month-to-date list price divided by the days elapsed, times the days in the month. It is a run rate: it assumes the rest of the month looks like the days so far, and it counts the first day of the month as a whole day. List price is what Claude Code reports per call, from its api_request events in Loki.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Projected savings this month
panels.description: Projected month-end list price minus the plan price: what the plan saves against paying per call, as a run rate. Negative means the plan costs more than the calls would at list price. Not shown until the plan has a price.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: List price as a multiple of the plan
panels.description: Projected month-end list price divided by the plan price. 1x means the plan costs what the calls would at list price; above 1x the plan is cheaper. Not shown until the plan has a price.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: List price through the month against the plan
panels.description: The Claude Code API calls at list price, added up hour by hour from the first of the month (the browser's timezone), against the plan price as a flat line. The day the list price crosses the line is the day the plan has paid for itself. List price is what Claude Code reports per call, from its api_request events in Loki. The plan line is the price as of now, and is absent until the plan has a price.

panels.title: Daily spend by cost center
panels.description: Every (service, usage type) pair mapped to a cost center by the rules in allocation.json; 'unallocated' is what no rule explains. This month and the three months before.

panels.title: Cost centers, this month against last
panels.description: Complete days 1 to N of each month. The footer sums the columns.

panels.title: Top rises, by service
panels.description: Services that cost more than on the same days of last month, largest rise first. A service on one side only counts in full.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(8, (((sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="this_month"})) or (sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="prior_month"})) * 0) - ((sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="prior_month"})) or (sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="this_month"})) * 0)) > 0))

panels.title: Top falls, by service
panels.description: Services that cost less than on the same days of last month, largest fall first, shown as the amount saved.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(8, (0 - (((sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="this_month"})) or (sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="prior_month"})) * 0) - ((sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="prior_month"})) or (sum by (service) (aws_cost_to_date_by_service_usd{period="this_month"})) * 0))) > 0))

panels.title: Top usage types this month
panels.description: Month to date per usage type. A usage type names the region, the instance size or the storage class; the resources row below goes one grain finer.

panels.title: Months by cost center
panels.description: Calendar months by cost center; the current month is to date.

panels.title: Months by record type
panels.description: Usage, tax, credits and refunds per calendar month. Credits and refunds post as negative amounts.

panels.title: Top resources this month
panels.description: Month to date per resource and cost center, from the cost and usage report's line items: an instance, a volume, a bucket, a distribution, a hosted zone, a model. One resource can sit in two cost centers (an instance's hours in compute, its bytes out in data-transfer). '(none)' is the lines without a resource: tax, API requests. The data row counts the resources and sums the ones beyond the list. Empty until the report's first delivery.

panels.title: Daily spend by resource
panels.description: Per UTC day, the costliest resources of this month and last, a resource's services added up (an instance's hours and its bytes out). Empty until the report's first delivery.

panels.title: Resources, latest day against their 28-day median
panels.description: The latest complete UTC day per resource against the median of the 28 days before it, zero-filled. Orange from 1.5, red from 2. A new instance shows here first. Medians under USD 0.10 count as 0.10 in the ratio; a line first seen on the latest day has no ratio.

targets.expr: max by (service, resource_id) (aws_cost_resource_latest_day_usd) / clamp_min(max by (service, resource_id) (aws_cost_resource_median_day_usd), 0.1)

panels.title: Services, latest day against their 28-day median
panels.description: The latest complete UTC day per service against the median of the 28 days before it, days without the service counted as zero. Orange from 1.5, red from 2. Domain renewals and tax are left out. Medians under USD 0.10 count as 0.10 in the ratio; a line first seen on the latest day has no ratio.

panels.title: Cost centers, latest day against their 28-day median
panels.description: Same test per cost center; here renewals and tax stay in, so 'domains-and-dns' and 'tax' spike by design on their day. Medians under USD 0.10 count as 0.10 in the ratio; a line first seen on the latest day has no ratio.

panels.title: Daily total
panels.description: All services per UTC day; the 'true' column is the days that may still change: the ones the report's latest delivery still covers, or the ones Cost Explorer marks as estimated.

panels.title: AWS cost per 1,000 searches, 7 days
panels.description: Compute and data transfer of the last 7 complete UTC days (ending yesterday, or earlier when the source lags) over the searches of the 7 days ending now: the two windows are up to a day apart. Everything on the box is in the numerator, so the figure is a ceiling.

panels.title: Claude Code cost per API call
panels.description: List-price cost over the number of api_request events in the range.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" [$__range]))

panels.title: Claude Code cost per 1M output tokens
panels.description: List-price cost over output tokens in the range, all models together; it moves with the model mix.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep cost_usd | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])) / (sum(sum_over_time({service_name=~"claude-code.*"} | event_name="api_request" | keep output_tokens | unwrap output_tokens [$__range])) / 1e6)

panels.title: Searches, 7 days
panels.description: The denominator of the search unit cost.

options.content: None in the account when this dashboard was built (the README keeps the date), so every hour is on demand and a coverage gauge would read 0%. At this size a commitment buys nothing; when the compute cost center runs steady for a quarter, `GetSavingsPlansPurchaseRecommendation` is the next call to add to the exporter.

panels.title: Allocated share
panels.description: Share of this month's AWS cost that a rule in allocation.json maps to a cost center. The rest is 'unallocated'.

panels.title: Days compared
panels.description: N in the this-month-against-last panels: complete days of this month so far, capped at the length of last month (28 or 29 at the end of March).

panels.title: Latest complete day
panels.description: The UTC day the anomaly tables and the latest-day stats describe: the last complete day the source has (before the day the report's latest delivery may still change).

panels.title: Data age
panels.description: Time since the report's latest delivery landed in S3 (up to three times a day; orange after a day), or, in Cost Explorer mode, since the exporter last asked for this month (every 12 h).

panels.title: Latest day estimated
panels.description: Cost Explorer marks recent days as estimates until it settles them; in report mode the latest complete day lies before the days a delivery may still change, so this reads No.

panels.title: Fixed-cost items without a price
panels.description: Items in the mounted fixed-costs file with amount_usd null. Enter the price and restart the exporter.

panels.title: Cost of measuring
panels.description: What this exporter's own Cost Explorer requests have cost, at USD 0.01 each, since it started. In report mode it only grows while a month has no report file yet (reading S3 is free at this size).

panels.title: Source
panels.description: cur = the cost and usage report in S3; cost_explorer = the Cost Explorer API.

panels.title: Forecast method
panels.description: run_rate = this month's complete days extended to month end; prior_month_rate = last month's daily mean when this month has no complete day yet; cost_explorer = Cost Explorer's forecast.

panels.title: Resources this month
panels.description: Distinct (service, resource) pairs with a line this month in the report; '(none)' counts as one.

panels.title: Resources beyond the list
panels.description: Month to date of the resources the resource panels leave out (they show the costliest ones of this month and last).

panels.title: Report line items
panels.description: Line items read from the report's latest delivery, all billing periods in the cache.
